tasks.title: Confirm ABDM callback signature scheme against the gateway contract

notes.text: INVESTIGATED, NOT CLOSED - AND IT CANNOT BE CLOSED FROM THE CODEBASE. F-003 asks for the scheme to be confirmed against the gateway contract; I do not have the NHA onboarding pack. Checked the implementation against ABDM's PUBLIC documentation instead and it almost certainly does not match. FINDING: AbdmCallbackVerifier expects a SHARED SECRET and checks HMAC-SHA256(secret, rawBody) hex-encoded, read from an X-HMAC-Signature header. ABDM's published contract does not describe issuing a per-HIP callback HMAC secret, and its callbacks carry Authorization: Bearer / X-HIP-ID / X-CM-ID - no NHA material mentions X-HMAC-Signature. The consent ARTEFACT carries its own signature verifiable against the Consent Manager's public key, which is a different mechanism at a different layer. WORSE: hms.abdm.callback.secret appeared in NO configuration file. It was unset, so the verifier was REJECTING EVERY CALLBACK - the ABDM consent integration has been silently receiving nothing. Failing closed was right, but the practical consequence is that whoever debugs the silence reaches for allow-unverified=true and reopens the exact hole WO-028 closed. DELIBERATELY DID NOT rewrite the verifier to a guessed scheme. Detached JWS is the pattern used elsewhere in the Indian health/AA stack and is a plausible guess; plausible is not a basis for an authentication mechanism, and a guessed check is worse than none because it reads as verification in every later review. DID: AbdmCallbackConfigCheck (startup ERROR + gauge hms_abdm_callback_auth_state: 1=open/bypassed, 2=closed-and-dead, 0=verified) so the dangerous states cannot sit quietly; and documented hms.abdm.callback.* in application.yml, which previously existed only as @Value defaults so nobody reading config could tell the endpoint was shut. TO CLOSE: three answers from the onboarding pack - (1) which header carries the signature, (2) what exactly is signed (raw body / JCS-canonicalised / detached JWS over selected headers), (3) which key verifies it (shared secret, or CM public key from which endpoint, cached and rotated how). Then it is a short change.

RESOLVED FROM PUBLIC DOCUMENTATION - no onboarding pack needed after all. The ABDM sandbox docs page 'Working with ABDM APIs' enumerates the headers the Gateway adds to its callback calls: X-HIP-ID, X-HIU-ID, X-CM-ID. Authorization is what WE send outbound with a session token from /v0.5/sessions. THERE IS NO CALLBACK SIGNATURE AND NO PER-HIP SECRET. So the original design could never have worked in either direction: with hms.abdm.callback.secret unset it rejected every callback, and NO value of that secret would have let a genuine ABDM callback through. X-HMAC-Signature was invented. The ABDM consent integration has been silently receiving nothing. REWRITTEN to what the gateway actually provides, weakest to strongest: (1) the callback URL registered against the Client ID; (2) X-CM-ID against an allowlist and X-HIP-ID against hms.gov.abdm.facility-id, both checked in AbdmCallbackVerifier; (3) CORRELATION, which is the real control and already existed unnoticed - AbdmConsentService.recordGrant throws when no consent request row matches the consentRequestId, so a forged callback cannot create consent from nothing, only act on an id we generated and are expecting. The HMAC path is retained but is now opt-in for deployments behind a signing middlebox, and a set secret now logs a WARNING because against real ABDM it closes the endpoint. HONEST RESIDUAL RISK: this is weaker than a signature and it is what the gateway offers. Someone who learns a live consentRequestId could race a fabricated grant against the real one. Mitigation is restricting the endpoint to ABDM egress ranges at the load balancer - documented in application.yml, not implementable here. AbdmCallbackConfigCheck updated: no-secret is now the CORRECT state and logs INFO, not ERROR.

tasks.title: Exercise key rotation

notes.text: DELIBERATELY DEFERRED. The POINT of this card is exercising rotation to prove it works. PiiKeyRotationUtil already exists and has never been run. Writing more rotation code without running it adds nothing.

LEDGER REPAIR: card id changed from M-003 to U-003. The old id collided campaign-wide and ledger.py resolved it to an older card in another work order, so this card was unreachable and any command aimed at it hit the wrong one. Documents updated in the same change.

REBUILT, NOT EXERCISED - THE CARD IS NOT DISCHARGED. U-003 asks for rotation to be EXERCISED; that needs a running app, a populated database and two keys, none of which exist here. What was done instead: read the existing PiiKeyRotationUtil before running it and found it would have destroyed the database. THREE DEFECTS: (1) the batch loop re-issued the same SELECT ... LIMIT 100 with no cursor and no done-marker, so after rotating 100 rows it re-selected the SAME 100 - now under the new key - and decrypted them with the old one; any table of 100+ rows failed partway with NO record of which rows used which key, and rotated vs unrotated ciphertext are indistinguishable, so the state was unrecoverable. (2) @Transactional imported and never applied. (3) It covered patients/users/consultants - 3 tables of 23 - so rotating then swapping the key in config would have made 20 tables PERMANENTLY UNDECRYPTABLE including every diagnosis, insurance claim and grievance. REPLACEMENT: PiiEncryptedColumnRegistry discovers targets by reflection over @Convert(Encrypted*) so coverage cannot drift; 23 reflected + 3 declared (patient_pediatric, sms_logs, template_data have no entity) = 26 tables, 74 columns. Keyset cursor committed in the SAME transaction as its batch. V221 progress ledger for resumability (no key material, no PII). plan() dry-runs the full round trip including a decrypt-back check and writes nothing. verify() re-reads everything under the new key alone. Already-new values are skipped so a resumed run is safe. Identical keys refused - it would march the cursor to the end and record COMPLETED, making a later real rotation skip everything and report success. BUG AVOIDED: the first registry attempt used regex over source and produced pharmacy_sales.sale_status, an @Enumerated(ORDINAL) column, matched because a @Convert on an EARLIER FIELD preceded it - rotation would have decrypted an integer. Hence reflection over field annotations, with a test pinning it. VERIFIED: 209 migrations replay clean; all 26 targets validated against the replayed schema - every one of the 74 encrypted columns and 26 id columns exists; 971 files parse. BEFORE ANYONE ROTATES: back up, STOP THE APPLICATION (rotation is not online - rows written during it use the old key and their table may already have been passed), then plan -> rotate -> verify -> swap config.

decisions.decision: The six F1 tables are tenant-wide (branchFilter 1=1); branch_id exists for the mapping and stays NULL.
decisions.reasoning: Branch-scoping an erasure request would let the statutory clock run against a record another branch's compliance officer cannot see. Branch-scoping the Rule 7 affected-principals list would mean under-notification. Retention policy is a hospital-level legal determination. grievance_events hangs off a branch-scoped parent that remains the access control, and a half-visible audit trail is worse than either extreme.

decisions.decision: A minor/DOB contradiction is refused, not corrected.
decisions.reasoning: Silent correction produces a consent record whose provenance is 'the server decided' while claiming a person attested to it. A refused capture is recoverable; a false attestation is the defect WO-022 already had to unwind.

decisions.decision: areas is deleted; customers is completed.
decisions.reasoning: Both were the same defect but not the same situation. V046 dropped the areas table and patients.area_id together, so the feature was retired and only the Java survived it — deleting matches the intent already expressed in the schema. customers is live, holds encrypted PII, and has a controller behind PHARMACY_SALES, so the table gets the missing columns instead.

decisions.decision: Tamil and Hindi notices ship as DRAFT with unreviewed translations, plus a language selector.
decisions.reasoning: Seeding without a selector would have left them unread, which is the same as not having them. Shipping them ACTIVE would be worse than English-only: a fluent mistranslation is relied upon and is invisible to everyone who cannot read it. DRAFT plus two named sign-offs is the honest middle.

decisions.decision: MFA is TOTP, and ships with mode OFF by default.
decisions.reasoning: The card was deferred five times because it rewires the authentication path and cannot be verified here. That reasoning still holds, so the design absorbs it: in OFF every path is inert and login behaves exactly as before, which makes this an unverified change that is not live on deploy. The operator opts in through OPTIONAL, watching hms_mfa_privileged_uncovered, before REQUIRED.

decisions.decision: patient_pediatric is encrypted in place rather than merged into patients.pediatric_data and dropped.
decisions.reasoning: Merging destroys data and needs sign-off; encrypting in place is additive and reversible while the rows are still plaintext. Two tables now hold paediatric data, one live and encrypted and one orphaned, which is a real trap for a future reader - raised as a follow-up rather than resolved by a migration that is not entitled to make that call.

decisions.decision: sms_logs is DELETE on erasure; template_data is RETAIN.
decisions.reasoning: sms_logs has no reader, no writer and no stated purpose, so there is nothing to weigh against the erasure right. template_data is clinical content hanging off an encounter that is itself RETAIN under medical-record obligations; deleting the template while keeping the encounter would leave a medical record with a hole in it, which serves the patient worse than either extreme.

decisions.decision: The login interstitial check is generic (any `status` field) rather than an enum of known values.
decisions.reasoning: Naming each interstitial meant the MFA ones fell through to a successful-login path, producing a UI that believed it was authenticated against a server that had created no session. A generic check fails safe for interstitials nobody has invented yet, which is the failure this one was.

decisions.decision: Rotation targets are discovered by reflection, never listed.
decisions.reasoning: A hardcoded list was wrong the day it was written - 3 tables of 23 - and would be wrong again the next time anyone adds an encrypted column without thinking about rotation, which is every time. Discovery removes the failure rather than documenting it. The three entity-less tables are the exception and are declared explicitly, because reflection cannot see what has no entity.

decisions.decision: The ABDM callback verifier is NOT rewritten to a guessed signature scheme.
decisions.reasoning: A guessed authentication check is worse than an absent one: it satisfies every later reviewer while protecting nothing. The honest move is to leave it failing closed, make the closed-and-dead and bypassed states loud enough that nobody drifts into the bypass, and write down the three questions that turn this into a short change.

decisions.decision: ABDM callbacks are authenticated by routing headers plus requestId correlation, not by a signature.
decisions.reasoning: The gateway does not sign callbacks, so requiring a signature is not a stricter policy - it is a permanently closed endpoint dressed as one. The correlation check was already present and is the substantive control; the headers are cheap defence on top. The residual risk is a forged grant racing a real one on a known consentRequestId, and the mitigation for that is network-level, so it is written down rather than pretended away in code.

decisions.decision: New tenants are seeded from a tenant-less template table, always DRAFT — never copied from another hospital.
decisions.reasoning: A consent notice is a statement by a specific Data Fiduciary about its own processing. Copying one hospital's notices into another publishes text the second never wrote, and carrying notice_state across means the first approval to ACTIVE silently propagates to every hospital onboarded afterwards. Forcing DRAFT keeps the human approval step where L-005 put it.
